Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Celebrates 20 Years with Blood Drives, Art Competitions, and Social Initiatives
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) marked its 20th anniversary on 19th Poush 2082 with nationwide programs. The bank organized blood donation drives at its central and regional offices, collecting 755 units of blood for local blood banks. It also hosted a nationwide art competition, “My Nepal in 2050 AD,” for students of grades 8–10, with 791 participants, awarding top winners with cash prizes.
Additionally, the bank distributed scholarships, warm clothing, stationery, sewing machines, and assisted in social initiatives like school support, Bagmati river cleaning, and aid for disadvantaged communities, including children with disabilities. The anniversary event at the central office featured the release of the bank’s institutional song, honored 47 employees with 10+ years of service, and included senior officials, shareholders, and clients.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Hosts “Muktinath Agri-Finance 360” Program on Poush 18
Full Content:
On the occasion of its 20th anniversary, Muktinath Bikas Bank organized the
“Muktinath Agri-Finance 360”
program on Poush 18, 2082, with the objective of expanding investment in agriculture, increasing productivity, and strengthening farmer's sustainability.
Agriculture and Livestock Development Minister Dr. Madan Pariyar, the chief guest, emphasized creating a motivating environment among stakeholders to expand the agricultural sector. He highlighted the need for credit guarantees, financial literacy, agricultural insurance, value-chain coordination, and collaboration with cooperatives and the private sector. He also stressed women-friendly agriculture, youth-focused employment through technology, and improved financial access for small farmers, noting that a new agriculture policy is forthcoming.
Special guest and Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development Dr. Rajendra Prasad Mishra pointed out gaps in the agricultural value chain and suggested that banks and financial institutions establish subsidiary companies related to agriculture, with coordination from Nepal Rastra Bank.
During the program Keynote speaker and banking expert Ajay Shrestha presented on challenges and opportunities in agricultural investment, citing high risks, weak credit quality, and low productivity, while highlighting opportunities through digital finance, value-chain development, agricultural insurance, and private-sector collaboration.
The event also featured a panel discussion on how agricultural enterprises can flourish in Nepal, with representatives from Nepal Rastra Bank, Agricultural Development Bank, FNCCI, and agricultural entrepreneurs. Around 350 participants from government bodies, financial institutions, cooperatives, private sector, academia, and media attended the program.
Muktinath Bikas Bank has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting rural development and strengthening agricultural enterprises.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Donates Motorcycles to Nepal Police for Enhanced Mobility
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has donated two motorcycles to the Nepal Police Maharajgunj Circle to strengthen public safety and improve police mobility and rapid response in Kathmandu. The handover ceremony was led by Deputy CEO Sameer Shekhar Bajracharya, who presented the keys to DSP Niranjan Thapa.
The motorcycles are expected to enhance patrolling, enable continuous monitoring, and support faster responses to emergencies in busy urban areas. This donation reflects the bank’s broader CSR initiatives, which focus on education, healthcare, disaster management, and public security, reinforcing its commitment to contributing to a safer and more functional society.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Approves 18.20% Dividend in 29th AGM
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) held its 29th Annual General Meeting on 15th Kartik 2082 in Pokhara. The AGM approved the annual report for FY 2080/081 and declared an 18.20% dividend for shareholders, comprising 13.53% bonus shares and 4.67% cash dividend.
Key proposals approved included increasing the bank’s paid-up capital to NPR 9,000,388,767.11, amending the relevant bylaws, and authorizing the board to initiate procedures for upgrading to a commercial bank as per Nepal Rastra Bank regulations. The meeting also appointed auditors for FY 2082/083. The AGM featured speeches from the chairman, board members, and CEO, and shareholder queries on the annual report were addressed.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of Fourth Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited third-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 153.74 Crores. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 131.04 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs.68.86 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 201.97% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 287.60% for Q4 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.04 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 4.92 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.03 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.9 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.17 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 90.12 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 4.1 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q4 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.82 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 32.18 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 97.52 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 69.32 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 546.93 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 4.55 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 3.64 Arba, and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank  with Rs. 2.24 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 4.47 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 128.34 Crores, with Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) also holding high provisions at Rs. 67.97 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 23.07 per share, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) followed by  with Rs. 21.82 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs.192.73 per share, followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) with Rs. 169.95 per share and Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) at Rs.168.13 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs.137.55.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 18.57 times, whereas Jyoti bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) reports the highest P/E ratio at 1248.34 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 0.28%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 50.97%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 31.54% while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the negative CAR at 7.84%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 6.61%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 3.87%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 89.62%, and Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the lowest at 63.04%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 16.24% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 6.02%. Meanwhile, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reports the highest interest spread rate of 4.60%, and Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has the lowest at 3.96%.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with MN Hospital to Offer Up to 15% Discount on Healthcare Services
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd. has signed a partnership agreement with MN Hospital located in Basundhara, Kathmandu, to offer special discounts on medical services to its customers. Through this agreement, customers of the bank can receive up to a 15% discount on various services such as surgeries, lab tests, X-rays, and medications.
The bank aims to make quality healthcare more accessible and affordable. Muktinath Bikas Bank has also pledged to continue expanding such service-based partnerships in the future. Additionally, the bank has recently launched the "Muktinath Faida App" that provides multiple benefits from mobile banking, along with cross-border QR payment services. Customers can now apply for loans, open accounts, deposit remittances, and perform various other banking services online without visiting the branch.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Undertakes CSR Activities Across Provinces
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has successfully carried out various Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives across different provinces, focusing on education, healthcare, and public welfare.
To support education, the bank provided school uniforms to 87 students studying at Shree Nawa Prabhav Basic School in Batala Gaun, Ward No. 5, Purbichauki Rural Municipality of Doti district in Sudurpaschim Province. The initiative is expected to encourage students and positively impact their learning environment.
In the healthcare sector, the bank donated 10 wheelchairs to Province Hospital Surkhet in Birendranagar-04, Karnali Province, aiming to ease mobility for patients and elderly visitors. Similarly, in Koshi Province, the bank handed over seven three-seater benches to District Hospital, Dhankuta, ensuring better seating arrangements for patients and caretakers.
The bank reaffirmed its commitment to continue making meaningful contributions in the areas of health, environment, and financial literacy, and to expand such impactful initiatives in the future.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches Digital Payment Service for Students Studying Abroad
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has introduced a new service enabling Nepali students to pay visa and educational fees directly through the bank, in partnership with Expert Education and Visa Services Pvt. Ltd.
The service covers payments for visa, exams, and application fees and is currently available at the Maharajgunj and Kamaladi branches. The bank promotes digital banking through its mobile app, QR payments, and various online services, aiming to simplify transactions and enhance customer convenience nationwide.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Conducts Financial Literacy Program for Startups and Youth Entrepreneurs
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited organized a financial literacy program focused on startups and young entrepreneurs as part of its corporate social responsibility initiative. The program aimed to enhance participants' understanding of financial management, banking access, business planning, budgeting, cash flow, credit mobilization, and consumer rights.
A total of 26 entrepreneurs participated in the event. The bank believes such efforts empower youth and promote sustainable business growth. Additionally, the bank recently launched the "Muktinath Faida" app, enabling users to access mobile banking, QR scan payments, online loans, account opening, internet banking, and remittance deposits from home.

Headline: Nepal Rastra Bank Takes Action Against Three Development Banks and Two Finance Companies
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken regulatory action against three development banks and two finance companies for non-compliance with its directives. Among them, Pokhara Finance and Janaki Finance have been subjected to prompt corrective action, while Muktinath Bikas Bank, Narayani Development Bank, and Salapa Bikas Bank have received warnings.
According to the NRB, the actions were taken following inspections carried out by its Financial Institutions Supervision Department during the third quarter of the fiscal year 2081/82. The inspections revealed several violations of NRB’s integrated directives and regulatory frameworks.
Muktinath Bikas Bank
NRB issued a warning to Bharat Raj Dhakal, Chairman of the Board of Muktinath Bikas Bank, for participating as the coordinator of the bank’s building construction committee. The central bank’s directives prohibit board chairpersons from being involved in any internal or sub-committees other than the board itself, a rule which Dhakal violated.
Narayani Development Bank
The Board of Directors of Narayani Development Bank has been found repeatedly breaching NRB’s directives. NRB has issued a written order directing the bank to immediately halt such violations. After being removed from the list of troubled institutions on Shrawan 21, 2077, the bank was instructed to raise its paid-up capital within two years, limit public deposits within 100% of paid-up capital, and cap single client loans at 10% of primary capital. However, the bank failed to meet these requirements and continued to collect deposits and disburse loans beyond the prescribed limits. It also failed to maintain the required capital adequacy ratio over an extended period. Consequently, NRB has instructed the bank to comply with the required minimum capital and capital adequacy ratio by the end of Asar 2082.
Salapa Bikas Bank
Salapa Bikas Bank was warned for failing to meet the minimum paid-up capital requirement and for ignoring multiple directives issued by the central bank. The NRB noted that the institution has not been adhering to regulatory provisions.
Pokhara Finance
Pokhara Finance was fined NPR 46,718.23 for failing to maintain the mandatory cash reserve ratio between Magh 13 and 26, 2081. Moreover, Ravi Chandra Gurung, the then CEO of the institution, was fined NPR 500,000 for failing to discharge his duties effectively. His explanation in response to the central bank’s inspection findings was deemed unsatisfactory. As a result, Gurung was dismissed from his post, and Prakash Gurung has been appointed as the new CEO.
Additionally, NRB found Pokhara Finance’s non-performing loans to have reached 33.44% by the end of Poush 2081. Its capital adequacy ratio was also below the regulatory threshold. The institution has been instructed to meet financial indicators within six months under the provisions of the Prompt Corrective Action Regulations, 2074.
Janaki Finance
Similarly, Janaki Finance has been subjected to prompt corrective action under Regulation 3 (Ga) of the same act due to its failure to maintain the minimum capital adequacy ratio as of the end of Mangsir 2081.
NRB’s actions reflect its ongoing efforts to strengthen regulatory compliance and ensure the stability of Nepal’s financial sector.

The agreement was signed by Muktinath Food Bank Director Mohan Kumar Basnet and Muktinath Capital CEO Mr. Kabindra Dhoj Joshi.
The advisory will also support restructuring, rights share issuance, and capital collection. Muktinath Food Bank plans to pass rights shares in an upcoming AGM and aims to issue public shares by FY 2082/83. Established in 2079, Muktinath Food Bank is a subsidiary of Muktinath Agriculture Company and focuses on quality, locally produced food products while supporting both consumer welfare and farmer market access.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches ‘Pocket Money’ Savings Account for Teenagers
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has introduced the "Muktinath Pocket Money Savings Account", targeting youth aged 15 to 18, especially SEE graduates. This account aims to promote financial literacy, the importance of saving, digital banking, and awareness of electronic transaction risks.
With a minimum balance of Rs. 50, customers receive free mobile banking until age 18, along with free financial literacy sessions, a Demat account, and MERO SHARE registration. The bank also promotes digital convenience through its Muktinath Faida App, enabling online banking services from home without visiting the branch.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with Southwestern Business College for Banking Literacy and Internship Opportunities
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank and Southwestern Business College have signed an agreement to promote banking literacy and business knowledge exchange. Under the deal, the bank will provide students with financial literacy programs covering modern banking, financial planning, and investment.
Additionally, qualified students will receive internship and training opportunities, enhancing their practical skills and employment prospects. The partnership marks the beginning of long-term collaboration focused on student development. The bank also promotes digital services through the Muktinath Faida App, enabling online banking, loan applications, and more from home.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches Financial Literacy Program Across Nepal
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) organized a financial literacy program across all seven provinces of Nepal in Falgun. The program targeted farmers, entrepreneurs, women, and youth, covering topics such as business planning, marketing strategies, budgeting, cash flow management, savings, loans, insurance, remittances, and digital banking services.
Participants expressed that such programs helped clear doubts and improve risk management. The bank emphasized the importance of financial education and plans to continue such initiatives in the future. Additionally, MNBBL launched the "Muktinath Faida App" for mobile banking services, enabling tasks like online loan applications, QR code scanning, and remittance deposits.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Supports 'Sundar Tulsipur, Surakshit Tulsipur' Campaign
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has extended its support to the
Sundar Tulsipur, Surakshit Tulsipur
campaign, initiated by the Tulsipur Chamber of Commerce and Industry as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) efforts. Under this initiative, the bank has provided financial assistance for the installation of CCTV cameras at various locations within the Tulsipur market area to help prevent and identify potential criminal activities and accidents.
The bank believes that this campaign, led by the Chamber of Commerce, will contribute to enhancing the security system of Tulsipur and provide a sense of safety to the local residents. In a formal event attended by Tulsipur Chamber of Commerce President Binay KC, other officials, and the Chief of the Tulsipur Area Police Office, the branch manager of Muktinath Bikas Bank’s Tulsipur branch, Saroj Kumar Lamichhane, officially handed over the financial support.
Additionally, the bank has introduced
Muktinath Saral Karja
schemes to promote small businesses under the slogan
"Nepalma Tikchha, Sajilo Chha"
. To encourage digital transactions, the bank also offers services such as prepaid dollar cards, mobile banking, QR code payments, online loan applications, online account opening, internet banking, and direct remittance deposits—enabling customers to access banking services from the comfort of their homes without visiting a physical branch.

Headline: Nepal Micro Insurance and Muktinath Bikas Bank Forge Strategic Partnership to Enhance Financial Inclusion
Full Content:
Nepal Micro Insurance Company Ltd (NMIC) and Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to collaborate on various business ventures, aiming to enhance financial inclusion and offer better financial and insurance solutions for Nepali consumers.
The MOU was signed by key officials from both companies, including NMIC CEO Mr. Mrigendra Rimal and Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd Deputy CEO Mr. Samir Sekhar Bajracharya.
The partnership will focus on expanding microinsurance services, creating customer-centric products, and promoting joint marketing initiatives, with a shared goal of driving sustainable growth and improving economic stability, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.

Headline: Comparative Analysis of Development Banks in Q2 FY 2081/82: Profits, Capital, and Ratios Unveiled
Full Content:
The second-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2081/82 have been publicly disclosed by 15 out of 16 development banks. These reports provide a comprehensive overview of their financial health. Karnali Development Bank Limited has not published its report as Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has declared it a "problematic institution" and placed its management under direct NRB control. Share trading of Karnali Development Bank has also been suspended.
This analysis aims to meticulously evaluate the financial performance of Nepal's development banks, categorized as "B" class financial institutions, using the unaudited second-quarter reports for the 2081/82 fiscal year.
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) currently lists 16 development banks, divided into National-level and Regional-level entities. Our focus is on assessing the performance of these "B" class financial institutions, drawing insights from the recently released quarter-end reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period, amounting to Rs. 54.93 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit, which amounts to Rs. 50.31 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 33.09 Crores. In terms of growth in net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) achieved the highest growth margin of 147.58% for Q2 of FY 81/82.
At the regional level, Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported the highest growth in net profit at 93.56% for Q2 of FY 81/82.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks, with Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) holding the second-highest paid-up capital at Rs. 5.68 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) reported the highest reserve and surplus, totaling Rs. 3.89 Arba. Following MNBBL is Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) with a reserve of Rs. 3.05 Arba. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) holds the third position with a reserve of 2.94 Arba.
Meanwhile, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU), and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
Among B-class institutions, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with a total deposit of Rs. 1.12 Kharba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a deposit of Rs. 87.33 Arba. The overall development banks have collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.99 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
As of Q2 2081/82, total loans and advances of development banks reached Rs. 4.75 Kharba, with an average loan of Rs. 31.70 Arba. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) disbursed the highest loan amount, totaling Rs. 95.64 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 67.66 Arba. Shine Resunga Development Limited (SHINE) disbursed Rs. 54.84 Arba, ranking third.
Net interest income:
In terms of Net Interest Income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) leads with Rs. 2.91 Arba, followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with Rs. 1.84 Arba, and Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) with Rs. 1.29 Arba. Out of the 15 banks, 8 reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside funds as loan loss provisions and delayed loan repayments for several borrowers.
Total impairment charges amount to Rs. 3.36 Arba for loans and other losses. Among National Level banks, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) shows the highest impairment charge at Rs. 82.72 Crores, with Shine Resunga Development Bank Limited (SHINE) also holding high provisions at Rs. 49.67 Crores.
At the regional level, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL), and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) reported a reversal in impairment charges.
Annualized Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the annualized EPS list at Rs. 19.34 per share, followed by Kamana Sewa Bank Limited (KSBBL) with Rs. 18.37 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) at Rs. 181.39 per share, followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with Rs. 165.35 per share and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) at Rs. 157.84 per share. The average net worth per share of the 15 banks is Rs. 132.15.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio indicates how much investors are paying for each rupee of the firm’s earnings. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio at 20.12 times, whereas Corporate Development Bank Limited reports the highest P/E ratio at 407.7 times.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loans indicate credit risk for banks. Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest NPL ratio at 1.74%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the highest at 43.69%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) reported the highest CAR at 35.21%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reported the lowest at 1.19%.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 7.17%, while Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest at 4.54%.
CD Ratio:
The Credit-Deposit Ratio shows how much deposit money has been used as loans. Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) reports the highest CD ratio of 88.64%, and Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has the lowest at 62.68%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
The base rate, the minimum interest rate banks charge, is highest at Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) with 15.91% and lowest at Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) with 7.21%. The average interest spread among development banks remains consistent at around 4.59%.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Concludes 18th Annual General Meeting
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited held its 18th Annual General Meeting in Pokhara, approving the Annual Report for FY 2080/81 and endorsing the issuance of NPR 1 Arba "8.5% Non-cumulative preference Shares", pending regulatory approval.
Key resolutions included appointing auditors for FY 2081/82 and relocating the central office to Lazimpat, Kathmandu. The bank honored 30 promoters, shareholders, and board members, reaffirming its commitment to growth and strong stakeholder relationships.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches Exciting "Anniversary Bonanza" Offers to Celebrate 19th Anniversary
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has introduced several promotional offers under its
Muktinath Anniversary Bonanza
to encourage digital payments on the occasion of its 19th anniversary. The offers, valid from
Poush 19 to Magh 19, 2081
, include a lucky draw for customers transferring funds via mobile banking, with two winners receiving mobile phones. Additionally, daily 19 users who top-up Rs. 100 or more will win a Rs. 100 top-up.
In another scheme, customers paying electricity bills via mobile banking can participate in a lucky draw to win up to Rs. 10,125 or their bill amount. Similarly, merchants using QR codes for transactions during a specific period can qualify for a lucky draw, with five winners receiving savings deposits. Customers making inter-bank transfers via mobile banking or paying bills using QR codes will also be eligible for daily cashback rewards ranging from Rs. 500 to Rs. 1,000.
To further promote digital transactions, the bank offers discounts for ATM withdrawals via VISA Network and has introduced the
Muktinath Faida App
, enabling seamless mobile banking, QR scanning, online loan applications, and account opening. With these initiatives, Muktinath Bikas Bank aims to simplify and encourage digital banking while celebrating its milestone.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Marks 18th Anniversary with Significant Initiatives
Full Content:
Celebrating its 18th anniversary, Muktinath Bikas Bank organized nationwide programs, including blood donation drives at its central and regional offices, collecting 611 units of blood for local blood banks. The bank also hosted a national art competition,
“Art for Earth, Combating Climate Change,”
for students in grades 8 to 10. Julen Gurung won the top prize of Rs. 50,000, while regional winners received Rs. 10,000 each.
In recognition of outstanding agricultural journalism, the bank awarded the
"Muktinath Excellence in Agricultural Journalism Award"
to Sagar Pariyar (Rs. 35,000), Kaushila Kunwar (Rs. 25,000), and Madhav Prasad Aryal (Rs. 15,000), along with certificates.
The bank also undertook various social initiatives, including scholarships for students, library support, warm clothes and stationery distribution, environmental clean-up drives, financial literacy programs, and donations for cultural and religious activities.
At the central event in Lazimpat, Kathmandu, Chairperson Bharat Raj Dhakal inaugurated the program, which included the launch of the bank’s anthem and the recognition of 41 employees completing 10 years of service. Board members, shareholders, customers, and staff attended the event.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank and Global IME Laghubitta Declare No Dividends for FY 2080/81
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has announced that it will not distribute dividends for the Fiscal Year 2080/81. This decision was made during the 340th Board Meeting held on Poush 01, 2081. The declaration remains subject to the approval of the financial statements by Nepal Rastra Bank and the upcoming Annual General Meeting (AGM).
MNBBL's stock closed at Rs. 388.30 yesterday.
Dividend History:
Similarly,
Global IME Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (GILB)
has also decided against distributing dividends for FY 2080/81. The resolution was passed during its 193rd Board Meeting held on Poush 02, 2081. Like MNBBL, this decision is contingent upon the regulatory approval of financial statements and the company’s AGM.
GILB's stock closed at Rs. 1,240 yesterday.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with Nepal Clearing House to Enable International Payments via Nepal Pay QR
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited and Nepal Clearing House Limited have partnered to enable international payments through Alipay Plus on Muktinath Bank's Nepal Pay QR and interoperable merchant QR.
This allows tourists from countries like China, Singapore, Malaysia, and more to make seamless digital payments in Nepal, enhancing convenience and reducing the need to carry cash.
The service is expected to boost Nepal’s economic and tourism sectors. Additionally, the bank offers discounts for fund withdrawals under the VISA Network and has launched the Muktinath Benefits App for added digital convenience.
The Muktinath Mutual Fund, Nepal's first collective investment fund, will be available starting Mangsir 20.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Expands Services with Health Discounts and Mutual Fund Offerings
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd. has partnered with Xeno Pharmacy Pvt. Ltd. and Nirvana Physiotherapy & Wellness Center to offer discounts of up to 25% on medicines and health-related services, including physiotherapy, osteopathy, naturopathy, and Ayurvedic medicine, for its employees and customers.
These benefits will be available at the pharmacy's Kathmandu-3, Lazimpat, and Bhaktapur branches. Additionally, the bank plans to sell units of Muktinath Mutual Fund, Nepal's first collective investment fund promoted by a development bank, starting in the upcoming month of Mangsir.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches "Muktinath FAIDA App" to Enhance Digital Banking Services
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has launched the Muktinath FAIDA App (Financial Access in Digital Application), enhancing its mobile banking services to promote digital payments.
The app offers a universal digital banking approach, allowing users to securely perform banking tasks from home. Features include setting security questions to prevent unauthorized access, seamless transactions using a single password across mobile and web platforms, and advanced security for device identification.
Additional features include bill payments, ATM card renewal, e-commerce activation, foreign exchange rate updates, transaction claims, complaints and suggestions submission, checkbook requests, and personal financial management tools like income and expense graphs.
Furthermore, the bank is set to offer units of Nepal's first mutual investment fund, Muktinath Mutual Fund, promoted by Muktinath Development Bank and managed by Muktinath Capital, through a public issue in Mangsir.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Honored with "Certificate of Merit" at SAFA Best Presented Annual Report Awards 2023
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank received a "Certificate of Merit" in the Financial Services Sector at the SAFA Best Presented Annual Report Awards 2023 held in Colombo, Sri Lanka. This marks the second time the bank has been honored, previously receiving the award in 2021 and 2023.
The award recognizes the quality of the bank's annual report, evaluated by the South Asian Federation of Accountants. The award was accepted by the bank's CEO, Mr. Pradyuman Pokharel. Additionally, the bank launched Nepal's first mutual investment fund, Muktinath Mutual Fund, which will begin selling units through a public issue in Mangsir.

Headline: Comprehensive Analysis of First Quarter Reports for FY 2081/82: A Closer Look at Development Banks in Nepal
Full Content:

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Launches First Mutual Fund: Muktinath Mutual Fund 1
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited has received approval from the Securities Board of Nepal to issue units for its mutual fund, "Muktinath Mutual Fund 1," managed by Muktinath Capital Limited.
This marks the bank's first collective investment fund in Nepal. Approved on October 23, 2024, the fund will issue 10 million units at NPR 10 each, totaling NPR 1 billion. Muktinath Bikas Bank and Muktinath Capital will acquire NPR 150 million in units, with the remaining NPR 850 million available for public subscription.
The closed-ended fund has a duration of 10 years, with investments in listed securities approved by the regulatory body. Muktinath Capital is responsible for managing the fund and has committed to ensuring sustainable returns.
The fund has received a "CARE-NP BBB (IS)" issuer rating for a stable outlook and "IRN AMC Quality 3" for asset management quality. A supervisory panel will oversee the fund, and public subscriptions are expected to begin by the end of Mangsir (December 2024).

Headline: iDE Nepal and Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd Sign MoU to Promote Financial Inclusion and Sustainable Development
Full Content:
iDE Nepal and Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd have signed an MoU to enhance financial inclusion, implement development programs, and conduct training and capacity-building initiatives. This collaboration reflects a shared commitment to addressing socio-economic challenges and promoting sustainable development in Nepal.
Signed by iDE Country Director Ms. Prajuna K.C. and Muktinath Bikas Bank CEO Mr. Pradyuman Pokharel, the partnership aims to improve financial inclusion, support rural development, assist smallholder farmers, ensure food security, adapt to climate change, and reduce poverty.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Promotes Financial Literacy Among Women Entrepreneurs
Full Content:
During the 21st Annual General Meeting of the Federation of Nepal Women Entrepreneurs, Muktinath Bikas Bank organized a financial literacy program aimed at empowering women entrepreneurs.
The program, facilitated by Deputy CEO Samir Sekhar Bajrachary and Marketing Head Binaya Ratna Shakya, addressed various banking transaction queries raised by participants.
Federation President Shobha Gyawali noted that the initiative not only encourages women to engage in banking but also prepares them to utilize bank loans more effectively in the future.
The event saw participation from 150 women entrepreneurs. To further support small and medium businesses, Muktinath Bikas Bank has introduced Muktinath Simple Loans and offers digital transaction services, including prepaid dollar cards, mobile banking, QR codes, online loan applications, and remittance deposits, allowing customers to access services from home without needing to visit bank branches.

Headline: Muktinath Foundation Celebrates Third Anniversary with Blood Donation and Dental Examination Programs
Full Content:
On its third anniversary, the Muktinath Foundation, a non-profit focused on aiding marginalized communities, hosted a significant blood donation and free dental examination program.
The event, which saw blood donations from 55 individuals and dental services provided to 48 people, was supported by the Central Blood Transfusion Center and Kantipur Dental Hospital.
Additionally, the foundation received financial contributions from its President, Bharatraj Dhakal (Rs. 10,000), Director Sitaram Kafle (Rs. 10,000), and Director Ram Prasad Pokharel (Rs. 15,000) in honor of their birthdays.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with Buddha Air to Offer Discounts for Customers
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has partnered with Buddha Air to offer discounts on air tickets for its employees and customers. Customers using the bank’s mobile banking or Visa card will receive up to an 8% discount on tickets bought directly from Buddha Air's counters, with the discount soon available through Buddha Air’s mobile app.
The bank, aligned with its motto "It’s Easy to Stay in Nepal," also offers various loan schemes like “Muktinath Saral Karja” and promotes digital transactions through services such as prepaid dollar cards, mobile banking, QR code payments, and more, aiming to enhance convenience and accessibility.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with Trishuli Beach Resort to Offer Exclusive Discounts
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd. has partnered with Trishuli Beach Resort in Galchi, Dhading, offering discounts of up to 150 on accommodation and food for its customers. To avail of these discounts, customers must use a valid bank debit or privilege card or pay through the bank’s mobile/internet banking.
Additionally, the bank has launched Muktinath Simple Loan Schemes to support small businesses and promote digital transactions through services like prepaid dollar cards, mobile banking, QR codes, online loan applications, and remittance deposits. Many of these services can be accessed from home.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Partners with Federation of Nepal Household and Small Industries to Boost Economic Growth
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank has signed an agreement with the Federation of Nepal Household and Small Industries to provide accessible loans and promote financial and business education for domestic and small industries.
The agreement was signed by Samir Shekhar Bajracharya, Deputy Chief Executive of the bank, and Umesh Prasad Singh, President of the Federation.
The bank will offer loans at favorable interest rates, based on business potential, and support entrepreneurs with financial literacy.
The bank's "Muktinath Saral Karja Yojana" aims to encourage small businesses, with services including mobile banking, online loan applications, and digital transactions available remotely, further simplifying banking processes for customers.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank and Chapakot Municipality Forge Agreement to Enhance Student Financial Literacy and Career Opportunities
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank and Chapakot Municipality Ward No. 9 of Syangja District have signed an agreement to conduct a financial literacy program and offer internships for students at the Chapakot campus.
The MoU, signed by Rishi Ram Dhakal, Regional Head of Muktinath Bikas Bank, and Poshraj Devkota, Acting Head of Chapakot Campus, aims to provide undergraduate students with practical knowledge, financial education, and career opportunities in banking.
The agreement, valid for five years, includes programs for internships and career development under Nepal Rastra Bank's regulations. The signing ceremony was attended by various local officials and academic staff, and chaired by Mukunda Raj Acharya, President of Chapakot Campus.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank and Federation of Women Entrepreneurs Nepal Sign Agreement to Boost Domestic and Small Industries
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank and the Federation of Women Entrepreneurs Nepal have signed an agreement to provide accessible loans to domestic and small industries affiliated with the Federation.
The agreement, signed by Til Bahadur Gurung from the bank and Shobha Gyawali from the Federation, aims to support economic development and enhance financial and professional education.
Under the agreement, the bank will offer loans at affordable rates to industrialists in 67 district chapters of the Federation and support financial and business literacy.
The Federation's president, Shobha Gyawali, expressed optimism about increased support for women entrepreneurs. The bank has introduced the Muktinath Saral Karja Yojanas to support small businesses and promote digital transactions through various online services.

Headline: Financial Showdown: A Comparative Deep Dive into Development Banks' Q4 Performance for FY 2080/81
Full Content:
The fourth-quarter reports for the fiscal year 2080/81 have been publicly disclosed by 16 development banks, with the notable exception of

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Appoints Umesh Kumar Acharya as Independent Director
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Ltd. has appointed Mr. Umesh Kumar Acharya as an independent director per Section 14 (3) of the Bank and Financial Institutions Act 2073. Mr. Acharya, with over 20 years in the banking sector and 13 years as a CEO at various financial institutions including Kamana Bikas Bank, is recognized as a banking expert and policy consultant. Full Content:
The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN) awarded Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) the Best Presented Annual Report Award for 2023 under the Nepal Financial Reporting Standards (NFRS). This marks the bank's fifth consecutive win for financial years 2075/076 to 2079/080.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Tribute to Late Founder President Khagendra Raj Regmi
Full Content:
The Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited held a condolence meeting at its central office in Lazimpat, Kathmandu, on Jestha 1st, 2081, to mourn the passing of founder president Khagendra Raj Regmi.
Attendees, including current and former directors, as well as central office employees, observed a minute's silence to honor his contributions.
Regmi's leadership played a crucial role in overcoming challenges and expanding the bank's operations, particularly in Syangja district.
Born on Shrawan 15th, 2006, Regmi devoted over two decades to teaching and social service, leaving a lasting impact on Syangja's educational, social, and economic development. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
conducted banking literacy programs as part of its financial literacy campaign, aiming to expand and promote banking services.
Programs were held at various locations including Saraswati Tika Secondary School in Pokhara-33, CCS College in Dhangadi-4, Star Foodland in Imadol-1, and near Deuti Bajai Mandir in Birendnagar-11.
These programs, attended by students, teachers, and locals, covered topics such as banking services, digital banking technology, and savings accounts.
Additionally, the bank introduced initiatives to encourage digital transactions, including the use of their bot for free withdrawals from other banks' bots nationwide.
Services such as prepaid dollar cards, mobile banking, QR codes, online loan applications, and missed call banking were also highlighted, promoting convenient banking access from home.

Headline: Nepal Rastra Bank Takes Stringent Measures Against Six Financial Institutions for Regulatory Violations
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken decisive disciplinary actions against six financial institutions, including Muktinath Bikas Bank, Saptakoshi Development Bank, Narayani Development Bank, Progressive Finance, Goodwill Finance, and Guheshwori Merchant Banking and Finance, for various violations of mandatory regulations.
Muktinath Bikas Bank, in contravention of the Consumer Protection Fund Operation Procedure, 2079, collected fees from customers for personal and group loans with the initial intention of benefiting borrowing customers. Subsequently, the bank diverted these funds for purposes unrelated to the collective interests of customers. Despite the claim of fund return, investigations revealed misuse, acting against the financial interests of depositors and the public. In response, the executive committee, chairman, and CEO of Muktinath Bikas Bank are now subject to caution under Section 100(2)(k) of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058.
Saptakoshi Development Bank, following a comprehensive on-site inspection, had its independent director's provision for the second term revoked due to lapses in decision-making. The bank's CEO is cautioned for unauthorized base rate changes and inaccurate submission of details on revised rates and loan information. Additionally, an independently appointed director, deemed legally incompetent, has been promptly removed. These actions align with the Banking and Financial Institution Act.
Narayani Development Bank faced penalties for failing to maintain the mandatory minimum cash reserve and exceeding the maximum limit of the Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio, resulting in a cash fine of NPR 12,846.28 and a penalty of NPR 2,41,924.01, respectively. These penalties are in accordance with the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058.
Progressive Finance Limited, after a comprehensive on-site inspection, received a caution from the Nepal Rastra Bank for adopting a risky valuation method in its lending to Maharjan Business Associates Pvt. Ltd. The caution is issued under Section 100, Sub-section (2), Clause (k) of the Banking and Financial Institution Act, 2058, emphasizing concerns about the decision-making process and collateral approval.
Goodwill Finance, following a special examination, faced a caution from the Nepal Rastra Bank for inadequate analysis of project viability and improper utilization of loan amounts when lending to Maharjan Business Associates Pvt. Ltd. The bank's management committee and CEO are cautioned under Section 100, Sub-section (2), Clause (k) of the Banking and Financial Institution Act, 2058.
Guheshwori Merchant Banking and Finance violated the regulatory framework by exceeding the investment threshold during the fiscal year 2079/80, engaging in excessive share selling. Consequently, the Chief Executive Officer of the institution is cautioned under Section 100, Sub-section (2), Clause (k) of the Banking and Financial Institution Act, 2058. Directives have been issued to ensure full compliance with all regulatory provisions in the future.

Headline: Nepal Rastra Bank Imposes Disciplinary Measures Against Six Financial Institutions for Regulatory Violations
Full Content:
Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) has taken stern disciplinary measures against six financial institutions, including Global IME Bank, Prabhu Bank, Himalayan Bank, Muktinath Bikas Bank, Garima Bikas Bank, and Reliance Finance, for violating mandatory regulations.
Global IME Bank (GBIME) is directed to refund excess funds charged as premiums, surpassing the allowed limits. The bank breached regulations by increasing the Risk Premium rate in the fiscal year 2079/80, contrary to the directive. The directive emphasizes the importance of setting aside funds for potential loan losses, addressing issues like misusing loans, inactive businesses, Debt-to-Equity Ratio non-compliance, and inadequate debt recovery.
Prabhu Bank (PRVU) faces penalties for improper loan classification and insufficient risk mitigation systems. Violations include incorrect loan loss categorization, failure to allocate funds for loan recovery, and an increase in the Risk Premium rate against guidelines. Additionally, inaccuracies in reporting loan risks under the Capital Adequacy Framework 2015 were noted.
Himalayan Bank (HBL) is under scrutiny for miscalculating its capital adequacy ratio, resulting in reduced primary capital and reporting higher risk-weighted assets. Despite holding necessary permits, the bank failed to categorize loans and allocate provisions as per Unified Directive 2079, Directive No. 2/079.
Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) incurs a Rs. 10 lakhs fine for non-compliance with ongoing due diligence. Directors of Garima Bikas Bank (GBBL) and Reliance Finance (RLFL) receive official warnings for regulatory breaches.
Garima Bikas Bank's Director, Dr. Ananda Prasad Shrestha, and others collected funds through a joint account intending to open an insurance company. Despite applications and funds from various institutions, insufficient oversight was noted. Dr. Ananda Prasad Shrestha is cautioned by NRB, and the CEO of the institution is also warned.
Reliance Finance's Chairman, Kush Prasad Mally, and others used joint and personal accounts for individual business transactions. Due to irregular Customer Due Diligence (CDD) updates and perceived weaknesses in institutional and managerial conduct, Chairman Kush Prasad Mally is cautioned by NRB.

Headline: Comparative Analysis of Development Banks in Q2 FY 2080/81: Profits, Capital, and Ratios Unveiled
Full Content:
The second-quarter reports for the ongoing fiscal year 2080/81 have been disclosed by 15 development banks, providing a comprehensive overview of their financial status. Among them, Karnali Development Bank (KRBL) stands as the sole exception, as it has yet to release its report. This analysis will particularly delve into assessing the financial performance of Development Banks of Nepal, a "B" class financial institution, based on the unaudited 2nd quarterly report of the 2080/81 fiscal year.
NEPSE currently lists a total of 16 development banks, each falling into distinct categories - National-level banks and Regional-level banks. Our focus lies specifically on scrutinizing the performance of B-class financial institutions within this framework, drawing insights from the disclosed second-quarter reports.
Net profit:
As per the quarterly report, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has reported the highest net profit for the period amounting to Rs. 51.26 Crores. Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) comes in second place in terms of profit which amounts to Rs. 42 Crores.
The third position is secured by Shine Resunga Development Bank (SHINE) with a net profit of Rs. 37.12 Crores. In terms of growth in Net profit, Jyoti Bikas Bank (JBBL) has obtained a growth margin of 190.73% for the Q2 of FY 80/81.
Coming towards the regional level, Green Development Bank (GRDBL) has reported the highest growth in net profit of 346.81% while Excel Development Bank (EDBL) reported the highest decline in net profit of 400.69% in the Q2 of FY 80/81.
Paid-up capital:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 7.05 Arba among all the development banks. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest paid-up capital amounting to Rs. 5.67 Arba.
On the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest paid-up capital of Rs. 26.25 Crores.
Reserve and surplus:
The reserve is the amount that is retained by the company from its profits to promote future growth.
Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) has reported the highest reserve and surplus which amounts to Rs. 2.73 Arba. LBBL is followed by Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) with a total reserve of Rs. 2.61 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has secured the third position with a reserve of 2.58 Arba.
Whereas, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) and Saptakoshi Development Bank (SAPDBL) have reported negative reserves and surplus.
Deposits from Customers:
In B-class institution, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has topped the list with a total deposit of Rs. 1.12 Kharba. This list is followed by Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) with a total deposit of Rs. 78.58 Arba.
The overall development bank has collected a total deposit of Rs. 5.65 Kharba.
Loans and Advances to Customers:
Till Q2 2080/2081, total loans and advances of development banks stood at Rs. 4.59 Kharba. The average loan stood at Rs. 30.59 Arba.
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has disbursed the highest amount of loans which amounts to Rs. 96.30 Arba. Following the list, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has disbursed a total loan of Rs. 63.91 Arba. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) has disbursed a loan of Rs. 50.81 Arba which puts it in third place.
Net interest income:
Net Interest Income is the core business revenue which is calculated by subtracting the cost related to the deposits from the income from loans and advances.
In terms of Net interest income, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) tops the list with a total of Rs. 2.08 Arba. Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the second-highest net interest income amounting to Rs. 1.80 Arba. GBBL is followed by Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) which has reported a net interest income of Rs. 1.12 Arba.
Out of the 15 banks, 8 banks have reported above-industry-average net interest income.
Provisions for the period (Impairment/Reversal):
Banks have set aside a certain amount in loan loss provision and have delayed the loan repayment of several borrowers. A total of Rs 3.19 Arba has been shown in an impairment charge for a loan and other losses.
In the National Level, Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has the highest impairment charge for a loan and other losses with Rs. 78.63 Crores. Jyoti Bikas Bank Limited (JBBL) also has higher provisions amounting to Rs. 54.75 Crores.
In the regional level, Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) and Sindhu Bikas Bank (SINDU) have reported the lowest impairment charges for this period.
Earnings per share:
Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) topped the list in terms of EPS amounting to Rs. 18.06 per share. Kamana Sewa Bikas Bank Limited (KSBBL) has the second-highest EPS with Rs. 15.78 per share.
Net worth per share:
The highest net worth per share is reported by Lumbini Bikas Bank Limited (LBBL) with Rs. 177.84 per share. This is followed by Mahalaxmi Bikas Bank Limited (MLBL) with a net worth per share of Rs. 154.04 per share. Similarly, Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) reported a net worth of Rs. 152.08 per share.
The average net worth per share comes at Rs. 127.45 per share when we factor in the net worth per share of 15 banks.
P/E Ratio:
The P/E ratio tells investors what they are paying for each rupee of earnings of the firm. The lower the ratio, the better the deal.
In terms of the P/E ratio, Garima Bikas Bank Limited (GBBL) has the lowest P/E ratio of 21.37 times. Meanwhile, Corporate Development Bank Limited reported the highest P/E of 110.11 times from the regional level.
One should always check the fundamentals of the company and if they find the bad fundamentals then there is a reason for the lower valuation. Also, the PE is calculated as per the quarter-end closing price of the respective companies. In today's date, the price differs in the secondary market.
Non-Performing Loans:
Non-performing loan indicates the risk of credit provided by the bank to its clients. A higher NPL indicates that the bank might be at risk.
In terms of NPL, Sindhu Bikas Bank Limited (SINDU) has the lowest ratio with an NPL of 1.05%, and on the other hand, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest NPL of 27.75%.
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR):
In terms of the Capital Adequacy ratio (CAR), Corporate Development Bank Limited (CORBL) seems to have reported the highest CAR of 44.77%, while Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has the lowest CAR of 9.46%.
CAR is the ratio of a bank's capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and current liabilities.
Others:
Cost of Funds, CD Ratio, Base Rates, and Interest Spread:
Cost of Funds:
The term cost of funds refers to how much banks and financial institutions spend in order to acquire money to lend to their customers. The lower the cost of funds, the better because it ultimately reduces the cost of banks. As per reports, Green Development Bank Limited (GRDBL) has the highest Cost of Funds at 9.32%, whereas Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest cost of funds at 7.44%.
CD Ratio:
The CD ratio refers to the credit-deposit ratio in banking parlance. It tells how much of the money banks have raised in the form of deposits has been deployed as loans. Similarly, Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) has reported the highest CD ratio of 91.20%, whereas Miteri Development Bank Limited (MDB) has reported the lowest CD ratio of 65.86%.
Base Rate and Interest Spread:
Base rate is defined as the minimum interest rate set by the NRB below which banks are not permitted to lend to their customers. Narayani Development Bank Limited (NABBC) reports the highest base rate of 17.64%, and Excel Development Bank Limited (EDBL) has the lowest base rate of 10.22%.
Likewise, the net interest rate spread represents the variance between the interest rate disbursed to depositors and the interest accrued from loans extended to consumers by a bank. Among the majority of development banks, a consistent interest spread rate of 4.59% has been upheld, with the highest reported at 4.60%.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Records 32.93% Q2 Net Profit Decline Despite Resilient Core Business Growth
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
has released its second-quarter report for FY 2080/81, revealing a 32.93% decline in net profit from Rs. 62.62 Crores in Q2 FY 2079/80 to Rs. 42 Crores in Q2 FY 2080/81.
During the same quarter, the bank reported a negative distributable profit after PL Appropriation and Regulatory Adjustments, amounting to Rs. 31.72 Crores.
Customer deposits experienced a 3.55% decrease, settling at Rs. 1.12 Kharba, while loans and advances to customers saw a 1.95% increase, reaching Rs. 96.29 Arba. Despite these fluctuations, the bank's core business income, represented by Net Interest Income, increased by 2.12% to Rs. 2.08 Arba compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
MNBBL's financial structure includes a paid-up capital of Rs. 7.04 Arba and Rs. 2.92 Arba in reserves and surplus.
The annualized earnings per share (EPS) for the bank stood at Rs. 11.24, with a Net worth per share of Rs. 137.03.
Notably, the company traded at a P/E multiple of 34.22 times. The Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of the bank stands at 11.25%. The Non-performing loan (NPL) ratio increased to 2.51%.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Concludes its 17th AGM; Endorses Proposal of 10.26% Dividend to Shareholders
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank (MNBBL) successfully conducted its 17th Annual General Meeting in Pokhara on the 28th day of Poush, 2080 B.S. The meeting approved the fiscal year 2079/80 annual report and endorsed a dividend distribution of 10.26% to shareholders. This dividend includes 9.75% in bonus shares and 0.51% in cash dividends for tax purposes.
During the meeting, Mr. Bharat Raj Dhakal, the Chairman of the Bank's Board of Directors, presided over the program. Mr. Gajendra Man Shrestha, a Board member, delivered a welcome speech, and Mr. Pradyuman Pokharel, the Bank's CEO, provided insights into the current status and future strategies. The meeting also addressed queries and suggestions from shareholders based on the annual report.
Furthermore, the Annual General Meeting resulted in the election of a new Board of Directors, including Mr. Bharat Raj Dhakal, Mr. Narayan Kumar Shrestha, Mr. Bharat Prasad Lamsal, Mr. Binod Kumar Sharma, and Mrs. Saroja Shrestha (Koirala). The selection was confirmed by Mr. Til Bahadur Gurung, the Chief Information Officer of the bank.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Celebrates 18 Years with Pledge To Innovation and Social Responsibility
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) marks its entry into the 18th year with a series of impactful programs, showcasing a steadfast commitment to innovation and corporate social responsibility.
In celebration of its 17th-year milestone, MNBBL has recognized and honored 135 dedicated employees who have contributed over a decade of service, demonstrating exceptional commitment through massive blood donation drives and various social initiatives.
Underlining its corporate social responsibility, the bank has extended financial support of Rs 5 lakh to the National Innovation Center, led by Dr. Mahabir Pun. This contribution aims to bolster initiatives focused on green energy, environmental protection, and plastic recycling.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Celebrates Anniversary with Exciting Customer Incentives
Full Content:
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL) has unveiled a series of customer-centric initiatives aimed at promoting digital payments. These schemes, announced on the occasion of the bank's anniversary, reflect the institution's commitment to fostering a cashless economy and rewarding its valued customers.
As part of the first plan, the bank is introducing a Top-Up Bonanza. From the 19th to the 25th of Poush 2080, customers making mobile banking top-up transactions of Rs. 200 or more will have the chance to win a daily top-up of Rs. 200 through a lucky draw. 18 lucky winners will be selected each day during the specified period.
The second plan targets customers paying electricity and internet bills through the bank's mobile banking. New business customers who make their first bill payment can receive 5% of the payment amount or up to a maximum of Rs. 50. Additionally, customers stand a chance to win up to 5 months' worth of bill payments or a maximum of Rs. 5000/- through a lucky draw. This plan will be active from the 19th of Poush to the 19th of Magh.
The third plan is designed for QR merchants associated with the bank. Merchants who conduct transactions of up to Rs. 500 through QR during the specified period will enter a lucky draw to win Smart Watches. This plan is applicable from the 19th of Poush to the 19th of Magh.
MNBBL is also facilitating digital transactions by allowing fee-free withdrawals from any ATM under the VISA Network. The bank encourages various digital operations, including mobile banking, QR code scanning, online loan applications, online account openings, internet banking, and remittance deposits from the comfort of customers' homes.

Headline: Resumption in Trading: NEPSE Lifts MNBBL Suspension
Full Content:
The Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) has ended the suspension on the trading of
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
securities. The company is ready to restart trading after a short pause due to the delayed submission of information on the dividend declaration for the fiscal year 2079/80.
NEPSE's official statement revealed MNBBL's failure to provide details about the dividend declaration in time, a requirement according to Securities Listing Regulations, 2075. Companies are mandated to furnish notices, information, and decisions influencing securities prices to NEPSE on or before the day of business commencement.
During MNBBL's board meeting on the 5th of Poush, the decision regarding the dividend declaration for 2079/80 was made. However, the information reached NEPSE a day later on the 6th of Poush, leading to an immediate suspension of MNBBL securities trading. NEPSE requested clarification from MNBBL within three working days.
MNBBL responded to NEPSE's inquiry, explaining that the delay was unintentional and a result of coincidental timing. They clarified that the discussion regarding the dividend took place during the meeting at 4:30 P.M. on the 5th of Poush.
Despite MNBBL's explanation, NEPSE, in its decision dated 2080/09/11, issued a warning to MNBBL and instructed the release of the suspended securities transactions. The warning emphasizes MNBBL's obligation to fully comply with the Securities Listing Regulations, 2075, and the terms.

Headline: Muktinath Bikas Bank Proposes 10.26% Dividend for FY 2079/80; Trading Halted as Regulatory Breach Unfolds
Full Content:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) has taken a decisive step by suspending the trading of
Muktinath Bikas Bank Limited (MNBBL)
following a breach of NEPSE rules. The suspension comes in the wake of MNBBL's recent board meeting held on Poush 5 at 2:30 PM, during trading hours, a violation of NEPSE regulations.
According to the recent notice published in NEPSE, the 311th meeting of MNBBL's board of directors convened to discuss the dividend declaration for the Fiscal Year 2079/80. The bank proposed a 10.2632% dividend, comprising 9.75% bonus shares and 0.5132% cash dividend (including tax) on the paid-up capital of Rs. 6.42 arba. However, the crucial misstep occurred as the meeting was conducted during trading hours, contrary to NEPSE's stipulated regulations.
As per Regulation 22(1)(d) of the Securities Listing Regulations, 2075, any notices, information, or decisions influencing shares' prices must not be taken during the time of trading. The untimely meeting and subsequent decisions by MNBBL led to a direct contradiction of NEPSE rules, prompting the stock exchange to suspend the trading of MNBBL. Now the company is mandated to provide NEPSE an explanation within 3 working days regarding the breach.

Headline: Government Records Rs. 12.5 Arba Profit Tax Collection from Mergers, Acquisitions, and FPOs as BFIs Meet Deadline
Full Content:
The Large Taxpayer Office revealed the collection of Rs. 12.5 Arba in profit tax from mergers, gains from acquisitions (bargain purchases), and profits derived from Follow-On Public Offerings (FPOs). This substantial amount was collected over the course of Friday and Saturday, with meticulous filings by numerous organizations.
On Friday, a total of 30 organizations contributed to this figure by filing taxes amounting to Rs. 11.3 Arba. The momentum continued on Saturday, with an additional 11 institutions filing taxes, totaling Rs. 1.44 Arba. Mr. Janak Sharma, the head of the Large Taxpayer Office, provided these details, emphasizing the proactive engagement of both public and private entities in fulfilling their tax obligations.
Crucially, it was revealed that among the 41 organizations that paid taxes on profits from FPO, 14 of them also paid taxes on profits from both FPO and bargain purchases resulting from mergers and acquisitions. The taxes collected fall under the purview of the current financial year, marking a significant boost in revenue generation.
The background of this revenue collection effort includes persistent recommendations from the Office of the Auditor General. Since the 57th annual report published in 2077 BS, concerns were raised regarding tax evasion related to premiums of FPO, gains from bargain purchases in mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales. Despite the repeated concerns, the Ministry of Finance and the Inland Revenue Department initially overlooked the issue.
However, the 60th report of the Office reiterated the importance of recovering revenues from these sources. Finance Minister Dr. Prakash Sharan Mahat responded to these concerns by introducing an arrangement. According to this arrangement, companies paying taxes in premiums of FPO, bargain purchase gains of mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales by the end of Mangsir would be exempted from fines and interests. The government intended to encourage timely payment of revenues.
This move faced legal scrutiny when 16 Banking and Financial Institutions (BFIs) filed a petition challenging the taxation initiative. The BFIs alleged that the government's decision to grant exemptions on fees and fines was unconstitutional, asserting that it amounted to imposing taxes against the constitutional framework. However, the constitutional bench of the Supreme Court recently dismissed the petition, upholding the government's position. The court ruled that the taxation did not constitute a levy on capital.
The formal announcement of the dismissal was made on last Thursday under the constitutional bench of Chief Justice Bishowambhar Prasad Shrestha, affirming the government's approach to taxation in this context.
BFIs were given a deadline to deposit the specified amount by the end of Mangsir, with the incentive that they would not be charged interest and penalties. As a result, companies proactively met this deadline, contributing significantly to the substantial revenue collection observed over the weekend.
